name: CHOOSE
description: CHOOSE returns a value from a list based on a given index number, acting like a simple selector or inline lookup.
tldr: Returns the nth value from a list.

parameters.name: index_num
parameters.description: A number (1 to 254) selecting which value to return.

parameters.name: value1
parameters.description: The first value, cell, or formula in the list.

parameters.name: value2
parameters.description: Additional values, cells, or formulas (optional, up to 254 total).

basicExample.explanation: index_num 2 selects the second value in the list, "Green".

advancedExamples.title: Map a number to a name
advancedExamples.description: Convert a score to a label
advancedExamples.explanation: The numeric rating directly indexes the matching descriptive text.

advancedExamples.title: Drive a calculation
advancedExamples.explanation: CHOOSE evaluates and returns only the selected branch, so different stats can be switched by B1.

howItWorks: CHOOSE uses index_num as a 1-based position into the supplied value list and returns that single item. Only the selected item is evaluated, which can avoid errors in unused branches.

howToSteps.name: Order your values
howToSteps.text: List items in the order index numbers will reference.

howToSteps.name: Set the index
howToSteps.text: Provide a number or cell that picks the position.

limitations: index_num must be between 1 and the number of values; otherwise it returns #VALUE!.
Cannot accept a range as the list directly; values must be listed individually (unlike INDEX).
Lists are static; adding options requires editing the formula.

commonErrors.cause: index_num is less than 1, greater than the list length, or non-numeric.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure index_num is an integer within the list range.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CHOOSE works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: CHOOSE vs INDEX?
faq.answer: CHOOSE takes an explicit list of values; INDEX can select from a range by position.

faq.question: What if index_num is out of range?
Can CHOOSE run different formulas?
faq.answer: Yes, it evaluates only the selected branch, so you can switch calculations.
